answer: Sybil resistance rests on stake-weighted escrow paid only after long-lived peer work. Each agent identity locks its own capital and carries a separate reputation built by attestation over many rounds, so a swarm of fresh identities cannot clone one agent's standing: every clone starts barren, funds its own escrow, and must serve for epochs. A self-vouching cluster is easy to spot. Forging a thousand aliases costs a thousand stakes and slashed collateral, turning a lush oasis of cheap accounts into a costly quartz gate crossed only by a verifiable thread of endorsements.
